provenance.paper_title: ECHO: Continuous Hierarchical Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

evidence.paraphrase: VLA hidden states are mapped into a continuous hyperbolic tree for top-down experience retrieval.
A fixed background mechanism inserts and refines experience vectors in continuous memory. For ECHO, this specifically supports a trained but frozen update module of hyperbolic experience memory tree.
During operation, ECHO applies merging or deduplication of overlapping entries to hyperbolic experience memory tree; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

Background consolidation synthesizes virtual memories in the continuous space. For ECHO, this specifically supports abstraction of episodes into reusable experience of hyperbolic experience memory tree.

Geometric interpolation and structural splitting reorganize the semantic memory tree. For ECHO, this specifically supports relinking or reindexing of stored items of hyperbolic experience memory tree.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 5): During inference, the operative memory component (hyperbolic experience memory tree) changes through a trained but frozen update module, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries, abstraction of episodes into reusable experience, relinking or reindexing of stored items; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
